title: AI-Generated Image Detection Using EfficientNet-B2 with RGB,FFT and Artifact Features
content: Images produced by generative models now look convincing enough that visual inspection alone is oftenunreliable. This paper examines a practical way to distinguish real photographs from AI-generated imagesusing an EfficientNet-B2 classifier supplied with complementary image information. The input includesthree RGB channels, a Fourier-frequency map, and an artifact-residual map. The evaluation uses 40,000labeled examples drawn from CommunityForensics-Small, divided into 28,000 training, 6,000 validation,and 6,000 test images. On the held-out test set, the classifier reached 94.53% accuracy (95% stratifiedbootstrap confidence interval: 93.95%–95.10%), an F1-score of 94.50% for the synthetic class, and anAUROC of 98.57%. The operating threshold was selected from validation data rather than tuned on thetest set. These results demonstrate encouraging performance within the sampled data distribution. They donot establish reliability on image generators absent from training, nor do they establish robustness to everyform of social-media processing. The study presents a reproducible detection pipeline and identifies thetests needed before the method can be considered a dependable general-purpose forensic tool.
